concept.title: PARQUET_BLOOM_FILTERING Query Option ( or higher only)

conbody.p: PARQUET_BLOOM_FILTERING query option The PARQUET_BLOOM_FILTERING query option controls whether Impala uses the Bloom filters stored in Parquet files to skip row groups when it scans Parquet data files.

When this option is enabled and the query has an equality predicate that compares a column with a constant value, for example WHERE id = 12345, Impala checks the value against the Parquet Bloom filter of the column in each row group. If the Bloom filter shows that the value does not occur in the row group, Impala skips the whole row group. A Bloom filter can return false positives, but no false negatives, so it never causes Impala to skip a row group that contains matching rows.

Impala uses a Parquet Bloom filter only if all of the following conditions are met:
The predicate is an equality comparison between the column and a constant value. Impala does not use Bloom filters for other predicates, such as range comparisons or IN lists with more than one distinct value.
The column has one of the following types: TINYINT, SMALLINT, or INT stored as the Parquet INT32 type, BIGINT stored as INT64, FLOAT stored as FLOAT, DOUBLE stored as DOUBLE, or STRING stored as BYTE_ARRAY.
The column chunk is not fully dictionary encoded. For fully dictionary encoded column chunks, Impala uses dictionary filtering instead, see .
Impala checks the Bloom filters only for the row groups that it could not skip based on the Parquet statistics.
In the query runtime profile, the NumBloomFilteredRowGroups counter in the SCAN node section shows the number of row groups that were skipped based on Parquet Bloom filters.
Impala can use the Parquet Bloom filters written by Impala or by other engines. To make Impala write Parquet Bloom filters, see and .
